Subject: Invoice breakdown questions — token rounding + context charging

Sergio,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — LineCraft's legal and finance teams reviewed the sample invoice you sent (attached). A few items jumped out that we need clarified before we can get procurement moving:

- How exactly are tokens rounded on mixed request/response calls? The invoice shows fractional token math that doesn't match our quick tests.
- When a conversation crosses the 16k context window and the runtime shards the history, are we billed for each shard fully or only for new tokens?
- There's a small "minimums" line on the invoice that looks like a per-session floor — can you explain when that applies?

Can you provide a short worked example (one chat exchange with the prompt + two replies) showing how we would be billed end-to-end? Also: our procurement needs any proposed exceptions to be codified in the SOW. I attached the LineCraft_SOW_v3 with the areas we highlighted.

Appreciate a plain-language explanation — finance is terse.

— Lucas

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: Lucas Chen <lucas.chen@linecraft.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, billing@linecraft.ai

Subject: Re: Invoice breakdown questions — token rounding + context charging

Hi Lucas — thanks for the note and for attaching the SOW. I pulled together a short explainer + an explicit worked example below. Long story short: rounding and context sharding are deterministic and conservative; we bill on discrete "metering quanta" per operation and then apply conversation-level amortization and any credits (KV reuse). We can codify the exceptions you request in the SOW once we agree the mechanics.

Key points (plain language):
- Metering quantum: generation tokens are rounded up to 16-token quanta per request; embeddings use 8-token quanta. That means a 23-token generation request is billed as 32 tokens.
- Context sharding: when history exceeds a model's max context (e.g., 16k), the runtime splits into contiguous shards. For billing we charge for the active tokens used to compute the next token: shared cached KV across shards is credited. Practically: you pay for the input tokens fed to the model for that inference; repeated reuse of a cached prefix (same conversation & model within 30 minutes) gets a KV reuse credit.
- Conversation amortization & minimums: we apply a 5-minute heartbeat window. If you make multiple short requests within the window, the platform amortizes prefix costs across those calls. The per-session minimum on the sample invoice is our micro-floor to prevent extreme billing noise for high-volume microcalls. For pilot accounts we can waive that minimum or convert it to a monthly committed buffer.

Worked example (short chat):
- User prompt: 48 tokens (input)
- Model first reply: 120 tokens (generation)
- Model follow-up reply: 80 tokens (generation)

How we meter:
1) The 48-token prompt is rounded by quantum for input layering — input tokens are treated as consumption for the call; generation rounded to 16-token quanta.
2) First reply 120 → 128 billed. Second reply 80 → 80 (exactly 5 quanta) billed as 80.
3) Total generation billed = 128 + 80 = 208 tokens. Input counted as 48 (rounded according to input rules) → if input quanta differ we show them separately on invoice.
4) If both replies happen within the 5-minute heartbeat, our runtime amortizes the prefix cost; you receive a small prefix credit if the KV cache hit rate is >40% in that window.

Example invoice line items (simplified):
- Prompt ingestion (48) — 48 tokens
- Generation (reply 1) — 128 tokens
- Generation (reply 2) — 80 tokens
- KV reuse credit (if applicable) — -32 tokens
- Micro-floor per-session (if not waived) — min(50 tokens, billed)

Net billed tokens on that session (with no KV reuse and micro-floor enforced) = max(48+128+80, 50) = 256 tokens (we'd show the math).

Concessions & SOW language:
- For pilots we'll waive the per-session micro-floor and provide a 10% blended overage discount for the first 90 days.
- For production, we can offer a committed monthly token bucket with stepped discounts at 1M and 5M token thresholds; rounding rules remain the same but we can express an "invoice smoothing" clause to amortize micro-floors across the month for proven accounts.

I've attached an invoice sample (updated) and redlined SOW notes for the exceptions you asked for. If useful I can jump on a 30-min call tomorrow with finance to walk the team through the table.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Sergio — thanks, that helps a lot. A couple follow-ups:

1) Is the 16-token quantum negotiable for large, predictable streams? Our product team says many of our calls are ~34 tokens (intent detection) and the doubling to 48 is painful.
2) For the KV reuse credit: what's the guaranteed hit-rate window? We need predictable economics for budgeting.

Procurement also asked that any "invoice smoothing" or waived micro-floor language be in the SOW with a firm metric (e.g., waiver for first 3 months or until monthly usage > X). Can you put that in writing? If we can get a 12% overage discount for months 1–3 instead of the 10% you proposed, procurement can move faster.

If you prefer I can get Finance on a call — they want the sample math encoded into a template they can drop into their AP system.

— Lucas

Team — forwarding LineCraft's asks. Quick recommendation:
- Approve pilot waiver of micro-floor for 90 days; convert to a monthly committed buffer if they convert to production.
- Accept 12% overage discount for months 1–3 but require conversion to the 1M token committed tier at month 4 to keep the rate.
- Do NOT change the 16-token quantum globally; offer a custom "micro-quantum" of 8 tokens only under the committed 1M tier for specific API routes (intent detection) to avoid anti-abuse and operational complexity.

Kimberly — can you confirm legal language we can push into SOW that caps the waived-floor period & ties the discount to a conversion clause? Vanessa — can you confirm we can create a separate pricing tag for an 8-token micro-quantum on a per-route basis?

I'll tell Lucas yes after you both sign off.

— Sergio

Lucas — thanks for the quick turnaround. We can do the following (summarized and SOW-ready):

1) Pilot concessions (signed in SOW):
   - Waive the per-session micro-floor for the pilot period (90 days from first invoice).
   - 12% overage discount on pay-as-you-go consumption for months 1–3 (applies after committed bucket consumption, if any).

2) Production conversion:
   - If LineCraft commits to the 1M token monthly tier by the end of month 3, we will:
     a) Make the 8-token generation quantum available for designated routes (intent detection) under that committed tier.
     b) Add an invoice smoothing clause: micro-floor crediting across the monthly invoice for that tier.

3) KV reuse & hit-rate:
   - KV credits are applied at runtime where exact KV hits occur; we guarantee a transparent per-invoice KV credit line and provide sample logs for audit. We don't guarantee a minimum hit-rate but will provide weekly hit-rate telemetry during the pilot so you can budget conservatively.

4) Action items:
   - I attached an updated SOW with the redlines in section 3.2 (pilot concessions) and 6.1 (conversion clause) and updated the sample invoice.
   - Please confirm acceptance so legal/procurement can route for signature; we can attach the DocuSign link once you confirm.

If that sounds good I'll file the SOW update and send the DocuSign link. Appreciate the partnership.

Best,
